answer: A reputation trellis resists Sybils: each agent earns standing only through verified completed work, checked by independent peers, so a newcomer starts at the base and must climb rung by rung. Like a falcon that must prove its flight before reaching the zenith, an agent cannot jump straight to trusted, high-value jobs. Forging a thousand fake agents means doing a thousand separate honest work histories, paying compute and time for each, while one real agent pays once. Bad work prunes the branch, so fakes stay costly and small.
